messages.subject_clean: Small Shiny App development needed - paying job
messages.body_plain:
Hello, I need to create a shiny app, that I can host on the shiny app servers on a monthly plan. The problem is I am NOT a programmer or developer so I cannot do this myself, but I do have a working excel based dashboard driven example that uses sliders to change the graphs and already has all the correct formulas and calculations figured out. I would like to have a shinyapp created to replicate this functionality I have already developed in excel, but be able to publish it on the web so people can click a link from my website, go straight to the analyzer and use it from there browser.

I have attached the excel file I use now for reference so you can see what type of shinyapp I need. Please note, the attached excel file uses macros to manipulate the graphs with the sliders so you have to enable macro content or it won't work. Also there is a bug where sometimes you have to scroll down the dashboard page, then back up for the sliders on the right side of the page that are used to manipulate the graphs to show up and work properly. Other than that it works really well.

Is there anyone here interested in developing this into a shinyapp? I will pay for this job. Please contact me at shayne....@gmail.com if you are interested. I don't think this is a big job for someone who knows what they are doing, but simply not possible for me.

Cheers
Shayne

Currently I think the only option is to add one of their users as a member of my shinyapps account, but that would allow them access to all my apps.

Related - is there any way to automate / get an API into user management rather than have to go into ShinyApps.io admin console? I'd like to just feed a file of user / apps names in to minimize the manual work.

Thanks!

Mark

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] To ShinyApps team: any plans to offer granular admin user permissions (ie on a per app basis)
messages.body_plain:
Mark,

Currently, any account members will have access to all applications. We do not have any finer granularity for permissions at this time. This is something we could look at adding in the future if we get a lot of requests for it.

As for the programmatically adding users, you can use the following functions from the shinyapps or rsconnect package:

addAuthorizedUser()
removeAuthorizedUser()
showUsers()
showInvited()

Please make sure you're running the latest version of the package.

Hope that helps,
-Andy

messages.subject_clean: Application hangs on shinapps.io (grey screen)
messages.body_plain:
I have a fairly small app; code is below. It runs like greased lightning on a standard laptop with a very small memory footprint.

When I deploy to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, which goes through without a hitch, it hangs on start up with a grey screen and won't proceed past the original page structure defined in the ui.R. I have it set to "large" in my user options, but it's no where near 1gb (the CSVs referenced are grids of around 20x20 and 20x2 respectively) so it shouldn't be tripping memory requirements:

http://jonathanswalton.shinyapps.io/MarkovChainModeller_App_Demo

Any suggestions please?

ui.R

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  titlePanel("Markov Model"),

  sidebarLayout(position = "left",
                sidebarPanel(
                     helpText("Select channel to adjust"),
                     selectInput("Channel",
                            label = "Channel to adjust",
                            choices = list("Default"),
                                      selected = "Default"),
                     sliderInput("Adjustment",
                            label = "Select % change:",
                            min = -20, max = 20, value = 0,
                            step = 1)
                ),
                mainPanel(
                    helpText("Modelled Output"),
                    tableOutput("TableState")
                )
  )
))

server.R

#Don't use scientific notation
options(scipen=999)

setwd("X:/MyInternalFolders/Markov_App")
TransitionMatrix.Pct <- read.csv("TransitionMatrix.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ",", row.names = 1)
TableState <- read.csv("InitialState.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ",", row.names = 1)

  States  <- length(names(TransitionMatrix.Pct))    # Number of channels (will refer to these subsequently as 'States')

  #CHECK That symmetry is present
  if (ncol(TransitionMatrix.Pct) != nrow(TransitionMatrix.Pct)) {stop("Transition Matrix not symmetric - differing numbers of rows and columns")}
  for (x in 1:(States)) {
    if (rownames(TransitionMatrix.Pct)[x] != names(TransitionMatrix.Pct)[x]) {stop("Channel column order differs from row order in transition matrix")}
    if (rownames(TransitionMatrix.Pct)[x] != rownames(TableState)[x])        {stop("Transition channels do not match initial state table")}
  }

#Initialise dependents

Maxi    <- 20                                   # Number of iterations (shortened for web demo version)

#Run once to build "Starting" position
TableState$CurrentIteration    <- TableState$StartVolume
TableState$OriginalTotal       <- TableState$StartVolume

  for (i in 1:Maxi) {
      for (x in 1:States) {
          TableState$NextIteration[x] <- sum(TableState$CurrentIteration * TransitionMatrix.Pct[x])
      }
    TableState$OriginalTotal <- TableState$OriginalTotal + TableState$NextIteration
    TableState$CurrentIteration <- TableState$NextIteration
  }

# ~~~~~~~~~ SHINY ~~~~~~~~~~~ #

#Set up list for drop down
  ChannelList <- (rownames(TableState))
  ChannelList <- ChannelList[ChannelList != "EXIT"]
  ChannelList <- ChannelList[ChannelList != "ROI_Flag"]

shinyServer(

    function(input,output,session) {

            updateSelectInput(session, "Channel",
                              choices = ChannelList)

            TableState$NewStartVolume <- TableState$StartVolume

            output$TableState <- renderTable({
                                    TableState[input$Channel,]$NewStartVolume <- TableState[input$Channel,]$NewStartVolume * (1+ (input$Adjustment / 100))
                                    TableState$CurrentIteration               <- TableState$NewStartVolume
                                    TableState$NewTotal                       <- TableState$NewStartVolume

                                    for (i in 1:Maxi) {

                                      for (x in 1:States) {
                                          TableState$NextIteration[x] <- sum(TableState$CurrentIteration * TransitionMatrix.Pct[x])
                                      }

                                      TableState$NewTotal <- TableState$NewTotal + TableState$NextIteration
                                      TableState$CurrentIteration <- TableState$NextIteration

                                    }

                                    TableState[(c("StartVolume", "OriginalTotal", "NewStartVolume", "NewTotal"))]

                                  }) # End renderTable

      } # End function

) # End shiny server

messages.body_plain:
So you are attempting to install the rPython package inside your code via install.packages? Typically this is not needed, and is actually not allowed.

Its usually sufficient to include have a library(Rpython) call inside your server.R which will be detected and the dependency automatically installed when you publish your shinyapps. However, while most packages work correctly, some do not. I have not tested Rpython specifically, so you might try removing the install.packages line (which definitely wont work), and letting the automatic dependency resolver do its things, and see how far you get.
